title: New kinds of task and the weak families: learning a new kind from few examples

brief.state:
B2 (3,302,481 params, from scratch: a 2-layer +-4-char conv reader with no attention, an 8-round looped thinker that writes a program run by an exact int64 executor, and a pointer-generator copy talker) has passed its 6-seed confirm on fresh seeds 200-205 (33-pc-confirm-b2; CONFIRM-ANALYSIS.json). Pooled-5 (6,040 rows) is 74.0 on average (73.0-74.7), against plain_tf 53.7 (+20.3, 6 of 6 seeds) and plain_tf_steps 67.1 (+6.9, 6 of 6 seeds). Chain-5 is 99.4-99.7. The verdict is PASS-1. PASS-2 is not judged, because the fine-tuned pythia-31m and 8-shot baselines were never run. Two caveats: the loops:0 leak check fails on 2 of 6 seeds (10.8 on seed 201, 5.7 on 203; limit 5), and the same seed leaks differently on different machines (seed 200: 0.0 on the PC, 1.4 on a rented 5090; seed 201: 10.8 vs 4.3).

The new-kinds problem is unsolved. The four held-out families average 1.6% (family split, 0-4 per family). The variant split (new layouts and new computations) is 34.7% right, so about 65% is missed; 11 of 33 families are under 20%. The clearest loss is fewshot_number_rule, where a rule has to be read from in-prompt examples: 22.7% for B2 against 37.6% for plain_tf_steps (-14.9). B2 also trails on rule_apply, order_chain, digits_parity, verify_claim and state_update. It wins on table_lookup (+4.8) and ties on group_induct.

No attempt to learn new kinds from few examples has shown a gain yet. Test B1 (10.9M students on teacher-written rows) was proved wrong (+0.78 against +15). C2 (rules from 3 examples) climbed on square and last_digit only. Job 8 nearly passed the multi-step climb (+10.4 and +9.7 against +10), and job 9 on six copies is running. A blind search with 6,000 guesses solves 77% of C2 questions, so C2 measures search as much as learning. Notebook and sleep variants score 0% on affine (a*x+b). No file measures accuracy against the number of examples per new kind.

Most queued tests have not run (queues 39-44 and the PASS-2 baselines in queues 30-31). The plain_tf_steps bar was trained with a 64-character cap that leaves 840 chain rows answer-only, which breaks rule 7. C0 is the test for that.

distinct.title: CPU probe: does B2 read the examples in its fewshot prompts?
distinct.summary: Run the saved B2 models on hand-built fewshot prompts and change one thing at a time: swap the example outputs for another rule's, swap the pair order, put the query first, drop to one example, split by minus sign, count how often the thinker writes any step, and feed it a hand-solved program. No training is needed. It says whether B2's 34.6 vs 60.8 in-distribution gap is a reading, position, sign, missing-program or digit-writing failure, and it routes most of the other fewshot ideas.
distinct.change: No model change. One new test script (hand-written scoring, allowed) run on CPU on B2_s100 and B2_s101 (/mnt/project-files/custom-io/checkpoints/29-b2-screen/, 13,243,510 bytes each, verified present), with plain_tf and plain_tf_steps seeds 100 and 101 (checkpoints/20-screen-s100-w1 and 22-screen-s101-w1, verified present) as comparators. Rows: 400 per stratum per seed, hand-built in the sk200k format '12->48; 18->72. Now 10->?' (research/data.md section 1) and in the own72 wrapper 'Examples: a -> b; ... Now q -> ?'; rules mult y=A*x (A 2-9), add y=x+B (B about -30..30), pair_sum; 2 or 3 pairs; prompts under 208 characters. Readouts from the same forward passes: (a) donor swap: keep x1, x2, q, replace the example outputs with another rule's, count answer follows donor / keeps original / copies an example output / unchanged; (b) pair-order swap (invariance share); (c) query moved to the front (accuracy drop); (d) accuracy at 1, 2, 3 pairs (4-7 reported apart, since training holds 2 or 3 pairs); (e) accuracy split by minus sign in the prompt; (f) share of rounds where the op head writes NOOP, the step-1 op chosen, and a hand-solved program teacher-forced through Ledger.run(gold=...) using the tensor layout of Ledger.gold(); (g) digit-error type among wrong answers (wrong length, wrong units digit, wrong tens digit); (h) add rows with B built in 1, 2 or 3 steps from {1,2,10,100} at k=2, inside the trained B range, as a build-cost ladder; (i) loops:0 lesion on the same rows as a control.
distinct.why: The brief's open question is whether the fewshot failure is in reading the examples or in writing the rule. Shown: fewshot in-distribution is 34.6 for B2 against 60.8 for plain_tf_steps and 62.9 for plain_tf, and plain_tf_steps gets no steps either, so the gap exists without steps on either side. Shown: the family has 0.0% program coverage and 96% of its gold answers are GEN mode, and rows with no program are trained toward NOOP at weight 0.1 with the gold NOOP teacher-forced. ORDER-BOUND: invariance share at most 0.70; ORDER-FREE: at least 0.90 and accuracy change within 3 points. POSITION-BOUND: query-first drop of 15 points or more; free: 5 or less. distinct.title: Examples-needed ruler: new number kinds, k from 0 to 7, with floors
distinct.summary: No file measures how accuracy grows with the number of in-prompt examples for a new kind, which is Ben's main measure. Build a fixed battery of about a dozen hand-written number rules never in training, ask each at k = 0 to 7 pairs, and score every model against a constant guess, a copy of the query, one blind search guess, a shuffled-label control, and the share of questions the examples actually pin down. Expect B2 to read near zero everywhere (a first honest answer: needs more than 7), so the main value is a fixed instrument for every later idea.
distinct.change: Test code only, no model change. 12 kinds (each verified in Python on 3,000 draws against the executor rules, 2-5 steps): square_minus_1 (x*x-1), cube, round_down_tens, tens_digit, triangular x(x+1)/2, distance_from_10 |x-10|, units_plus_tens, digit_product, reverse2, hidden_k_reverse_sub (y = k - x with k from the pair), divide_by_hidden_k (exact), and pair_product (a,b)->a*b. Prompt 'Examples: x1 -> y1; ...; Now xq -> ?'. Slot limit: single-input prompts use 2k+1 of the 16 number slots so k <= 7; tuple prompts use 3k+2 so k <= 4. No negative numbers and no other numbers in the prompt. A kind stays only if blind breadth-first search (9 ops, at most 7 steps, prompt numbers plus 1, 2, 10, 100, exact DIV, 6,000 programs) reaches 80% at k=7 on DEV. 40 rows per (kind, k) on DEV, 100 per cell sealed by hash before any run. Floors per cell: constant guess, copy-query, repeat-last-output, blind first-fit at 1, 4 and 32 guesses, pinned share (all fitting programs agree on the query), shuffled-label control (outputs permuted by a derangement, scored against the true key). Headline k_half = smallest k where the pooled curve is halfway from the best non-search floor to the model's own k=7 accuracy, reported only if k=7 clears that floor by 20 points; excess area over log2 k as companion. Also tabulate, labelled C2 and apart, blind-search determinacy at k = 1..4 for the five C2 held-out kinds (blind_baseline.search_fits) as a ceiling table.
distinct.why: Shown: the only example-count results are k=2 (fewshot family, B2 22.7 pooled-5 vs 37.7 plain_tf) and k=3 (C2); blind search with a checker already solves 77.3% of C2 at 6,000 guesses, so a model must be read against search and against shortcuts, not against chance. Shown: B2 reads only the first 16 numbers, so a k=8 prompt puts the query out of reach. Single-input training prompts hold 2 or 3 pairs only, so k>=4 also tests length, and k<=3 and k>=4 are reported apart.

distinct.title: Hand-written read-then-apply traces for fewshot add and mult
distinct.summary: The biggest B2 loss is fewshot_number_rule (34.6 vs 60.8 in distribution), and B2 gets no program for it, so its exact calculator never runs and the answer is spelled digit by digit from nine registers. Give each add and mult row a two-step hand-written trace (divide or subtract the first example's output by its input, then apply to the query) that the existing parser already reads. The answer then becomes an executed result slot instead of a latent guess, with zero new parameters.
distinct.change: Teaching data only, on the skills-build branch (the generator is not in this checkout, so a rebuild comes first; research/data.md says --dev-per-cell 200 reproduces the train hash). For each add or mult fewshot row replace the steps text ('rule x*A+B' and 'infer pair rule' both raise 'unparsed step' in progparse.to_program today) with: mult 'y1 / x1 = A' then 'xq * A = answer' (e.g. '48 / 12 = 4; 10 * 4 = 40'); add 'y1 - x1 = B' then 'xq + B = answer'. Operands resolve by value to prompt slots (progparse.Builder). Use a random example pair per epoch only in a later arm. pair_sum keeps no trace in the first arm (a 1-step ADD trace would teach 'tuple means ADD'; report pair_sum apart). Rows whose prompt contains a minus sign (11.9% of fewshot, all add) stay answer-only in this arm and are disclosed, because the unsigned number reader drops the sign; affine rows are not traced (variant stays zero-shot). Free pre-check before training: the trace reproduces the gold answer on 100% of unsigned add and mult train rows, every traced row has at most 2 steps, and the untraced rows are counted. Matched control: plain_tf_steps with fewshot_number_rule added to STEP_FAMILIES and the same trace text (each target is about 30 characters, under its 64-character cap). Parameters: 0 (B2 stays 3,302,481).
distinct.why: Shown: fewshot has 0.0% program coverage, so its op head is trained toward NOOP at weight 0.1 and the answer is written in GEN mode from registers; chain families that do have programs reach 99.4-99.7 chain-5. Shown (existence check on 46,618 pool rows): the two-step trace on prompt-number slots reproduces the gold answer on 88.1% of rows (add 9,475 of 9,475 sign-free rows, mult 16,288 of 16,288, pair_sum 15,312 of 15,312) and fails only where the minus sign is lost (only 1,681 of 5,543 negative add rows come out right). The op head's answer loss cannot reach the op choice (the executor is integer and the op enters as an argmax), so without traces the thinker is never taught to compute here. Suggested mechanism: once the rate or offset is an exact result slot, the thinker only has to bind it to the query, which chain families already do.

distinct.title: Candidate-then-check traces: let the executor pick add or mult
distinct.summary: After plain traces teach read-then-apply, the remaining decision is which rule (divide or subtract) the examples support. Instead of making the thinker guess it from digits, write traces that run both candidates on the examples and let the executor's own valid bit (exact division works or not) or a replay residual choose, so the choice is read from computed results. The same idea scales to a made-up operator word: run all four basic ops on one worked example and copy the op whose result matches.
distinct.change: Teaching data plus one parser pattern (progparse: 'a / b = ?' writes a DIV step with no value; ex('DIV') returns None for an inexact division today and to_program raises). Arm B (both-branch): add trace ['33 / 24 = ?', '29 / 20 = ?', '30 / 21 = ?', '33 - 24 = 9', '29 + 9 = 38']; mult trace ['108 / 27 = 4', '92 / 23 = 4', '84 / 21 = 4', '108 - 27 = 81', '6 * 4 = 24']; steps 1-4 are identical for both rules, step 5 picks ADD or MUL from the valid bits of slots 20-22 (5 of 7 result slots). Arm D (replay gate): offset on example 1, replay on example 2, residual = replay minus the true output; step 5 is ADD if the residual is zero, MUL by the factor otherwise (mult never repeats an example input, so its residual is never zero). Arm N (nonce operator, from w1e-3): 'a W b = c' one worked example with W from 40 made-up words, four candidate steps ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV on the example operands, then the query step with the op whose result equals c (coincidence rows filtered); 20 sealed nonce words never trained. distinct.summary: Train on episodes whose hidden rule is shown only through 2-4 examples, built from known pieces, with some composition held out (mul-then-add, the affine shape) and some rule kinds fully sealed, then score at k = 1, 2, 4, 8 examples. Do it only after the base fewshot reading works, because B2 currently reads even its trained fewshot rules poorly.
distinct.change: Data mix of about 10% of each batch (or 6, 8 and 12 primitives as a diversity sweep). Numeric arm (screen on plain_tf, answer-only, no step parser): primitives x*k, x+k, x-k, exact x/k, max(x,k), min(x,k); episodes are ordered pairs of two primitives shown by 2-3 examples; the ordered pair (x*k then x+k) is held out; 6, 8 and 12 primitives give 30, 56 and 132 ordered pairs. k-spread arm: k drawn 1-5 per row (vs k=3 only) using C2 add and mult rows. Symbol arm (B2): letter-string rules (swap two letters, move first letter to the end, double each letter, drop every second letter, sort the letters) from 2-4 pairs, with three further kinds sealed and scored at k = 1, 2, 4, 8, 60 rows per kind and k. distinct.title: Key-free sleep controls: stop rule, harm guard, replay bank, dose
distinct.summary: The C2 loop sleeps exactly two nights and every keep, dose and harm decision reads keyed skills data. Test whether the model's own key-free signals can replace them: reach@4 from the example check alone tracks the keyed score closely across 16 dose settings (Spearman 0.87), and agreement with the model's own pre-sleep answers on unlabelled old questions might track keyed harm (the earlier key-free proxy, fresh add/mult fit rate, does not: Spearman -0.13). Replay of the model's own verified finds, a plateau-based dose and gap-driven practice weights are follow-ups.
distinct.change: Primary 1 (stop): in c2_stuck.run loop nights 1-4 instead of 1-2; after each night measure reach@4 on the 256 DEV questions by example check only; keep sleeping while it gains at least 1 point (cap 4); keep the best key-free night; log keyed scores for reference only. Primary 2 (harm guard): before each sleep store the model's greedy answers on about 512 unlabelled old questions; after the sleep re-answer; if the changed share exceeds a threshold fixed before shipping keep the pre-sleep copy; re-run the 8 dose settings per parent. Follow-ups: replay bank of the model's own executor-verified tries (at most 2 per question) instead of 2,048 solver add/mult rows, with an agreement monitor; plateau dose (double executor draws until a held-out set of fresh draws stops improving, 95% interval of the last doubling includes zero); sleep weight proportional to failure share on the model's own draws per behaviour class, with a 10% floor and a drop rule.
distinct.why: Shown: night 2 added +6.5 and +5.2 points on multi-step kinds over night 1, so nights 3 and 4 were never tested; across 16 dose settings keyed harm runs 0.2-4.3 points. The stepping-stone sleep took fresh add/mult reach@32 from 61% / 57% to 11% / 11%, and replaying solver rows restored it, so the replay source and the harm guard matter for rule 10. Affine is not expected to move under any of these.
